newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: FDA grants approvable status for Elan's Carbatrol.
newsitem.headline: FDA grants approvable status for Elan's Carbatrol.

text.p: Elan Corp Plc said on Tuesday that Shire Laboratories Inc had received an approvable letter for its product Carbatrol from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).
The letter states that Carbatrol is indicated for use in patients with epilepsy and as a specific analgesic for trigeminal neuralgia, Elan said in a statement.
Final approval of the new drug application is contingent on finalising the labelling for Carbatrol and certain other chemistry, manufacturing and control issues, Elan said.
Shire entered into an exclusive world-wide licence for Carbatrol with Elan's wholly-owned subsidiary Athena Neurosciences.

"We believe that the capsule technology utilised by Carbatrol represents a real advantage to the people who take this medication and will be an important addition to Elan's growing line of treatments for epilepsy," Athena's president and chief operating officer Michael D. Coffee said.
Carbatrol represents the second anti-convulsant to be marketed by Elan that has received an approvable letter.
Diastat was deemed approvable by the FDA in December 1996.
Both products, upon final FDA approval, will be marketed in the U.S. through Athena's specialised field sales force, Elan said.
